name: Rocket ridge
description: Longer terrain for 800-unit firing, asymmetric approaches and mixed weapons.

scenarios.name: Rockets: Blue nearer
scenarios.description: Blue starts on the rising side; Red approaches over flatter ground. Both stop to aim once an clear firing solution is possible.

scenarios.name: Rockets: Red nearer
scenarios.description: Mirrored uneven approach: Red is nearer the ridge. Watch variable angles, committed arcs and range scatter.

scenarios.name: Red rocket holds crest
scenarios.description: Red holds the ridge; Blue approaches from from lower ground, then stops to aim uphill.

scenarios.name: Blue rocket holds crest
scenarios.description: Blue holds the ridge; Red approaches from from lower ground, then stops to aim uphill.

scenarios.name: Blue rocket vs rifle
scenarios.description: A Blue rocketeer approaches the ridge while a Red rifleman keeps advancing. Rifle bullets follow their actual uphill/downhill direction.

scenarios.name: Red rocket vs rifle
scenarios.description: Mirrored mixed-weapons approach. The rifle keeps walking; the rocket launcher stops to aim and lead current movement.

scenarios.name: 800-unit rocket exchange
scenarios.description: Both hold exactly 800 units apart. Equal-ground reach is approximately800; scatter can exceed available power. The solver attempts the quickest feasible clear arc.

scenarios.name: Blue high: 860 units
scenarios.description: Blue is180 units higher. At860 separation, Blue can arc downhill while Red cannot reach uphill. Compare actual clear shots and approximate clear-air reach.

scenarios.name: Red high: 860 units
scenarios.description: Mirrored height advantage: Red can fire860 units downhill. Blue has the same weapon power but cannot yet reach uphill.

scenarios.name: Flat: 860 out of reach
scenarios.description: Both stand at equal ground height860 units apart. The same launch power reaches approximately800 on flat ground; no arbitrary distance cap decides eligibility.
